data.narrative:
Stratek Global is a growth-stage nuclear energy company founded by Kelvin Kemm. The valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of 8 peers—3 public (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 5 private (Oklo, X-Energy, Nano Nuclear Energy, Fuse Energy, Blue Energy)—all operating in the nuclear energy sector.

The peer-median method is inapplicable due to insufficient narrow-stage matches. Of 4 same-sector peers identified, none qualified under same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier filters, falling short of the required 3-datapoint threshold. Applying an all-sector median would introduce material bias and was rejected.

With triangulation methods yielding no quantified results, a defensible valuation range cannot be derived from the supplied data. The analysis is constrained by the absence of stage-comparable transaction data and publicly disclosed private valuations for near-peers. Key uncertainties include Stratek's technology maturity relative to the peer set, capital efficiency, regulatory pathway clarity, and commercial timeline—none of which are specified. Additional disclosure on recent funding rounds, revenue run rate, or capital requirements for the next development phase would be necessary to anchor a rigorous valuation. The composition of the comp set suggests the nuclear energy subsector is emerging but data-sparse for growth-stage private companies.
